data.name: Tango Fiesta
data.detailed_description:
Tango Fiesta is an action packed top-down cooperative two stick shooter for 1 to 4 players. Set in a world where the events from every single 80’s action film ever made actually happened to one unlucky hero called John Strong, you and up to three friends get to blast, shoot, knife, and high score your way through endless procedurally generated levels in the ultimate true story behind all those amazing movies!




What’s in Tango Fiesta right now? All of this...

6 CLASSIC ACTION HEROES TO CHOOSE FROM!


JOHN STRONG! The world’s least-known most-dangerous man.
MACMILLAN! John’s best friend and comrade in arms.
BIONIC COP! He thinks he’s a Cop. He thinks he’s a robot. But is he either? Both? NEITHER?


CONCHITA! Five feet three inches of pure dynamite, this wrongly-convicted felon is out to prove her innocence by killing everyone in her way.
DR HENK! he’s a doctor of parapsychology don't you know? He loves bustin' too, and this hobby just became his only means of survival!
MILLER! A slightly scary Australian man with a nice jacket and an even nicer sawn-off shotgun.

4 PLAYERLOCAL COOPERATIVE PLAY!

Team up with your friends to deal out death and destruction to the endless hordes!

ENDLESS PROCEDURAL CHALLENGE!

Five worlds of procedurally generated mayhem means no two plays are ever the same across all 20 stages! 17 enemy types keep the action challenging and fresh!

Take in the sun (and avoid the bullets) on the golden sandy beaches of Gordon’s Island!


Dive for cover in the usefully-tough foliage that grows in the Central American Jungle!


Prove your innocence by killing your way through the fiendish death mazes in the world’s most popular TV show, Who Wants To Be A Killionaire!


Don't cross the streams! Busting ghouls and ghosts in the spooky, fog-laden Ghoul Squad!


Define the future of law enforcement fighting through the rust belts riddled through future Detroit!

SHOCKS, TWISTS AND TURNS IN STORY MODE!


Although our main inspirations are better known for their snappy one liners over their well developed character arcs we’re taking the opportunity to set the world to rights. Help John Strong as he unveils the true story behind all of your favourite classic 1980’s action flicks. Go with him if you want to believe!

SUPER EVIL BOSSES!


Every Quaid needs his Richter. Every Ripley needs her Alien Queen. Every Matrix needs his Bennett. We’re going to cover you in so many iconic, hilarious, over the top and challenging bosses you’ll wish you’d never promised to save the world.

MASSIVE ARSENAL!


Will you choose the Oozy 9mm, Arius A1, Matrix 80, Sawn-off, Viper Combat Rifle, or one of the other 25 to crush your enemies with? Say hello to every little friend you could ever want - unlock them through play and then buy them for your hero!

FULLY DESTRUCTIBLE SCENERY!


Our heroes ain’t got time to bleed, but the rest of the world doesn’t get off so lightly. Getting overrun? Destroy those Spawn Huts to stem the tide of bad guys. Stuck between a rock and a hard place? Blast your way through any wall or structure - show those bricks who’s boss!

Imagine the events from every single 80’s action film ever made really happened to one guy - you & up to 3 friends get to blast, shoot & knife your way through procedurally generated levels as the ultimate one (or 2, 3, or 4) man army!

reviews.review:
Tango Fiesta is an energetic twin-stick shooter that transforms the spirit of classic 1980s action films into a fast-paced arcade experience. Developed by Spilt Milk Studios and published by Mastertronic, the game embraces the larger-than-life style of action cinema, delivering an adventure filled with explosions, endless gunfire, and exaggerated heroes. Rather than taking a realistic approach to combat, it focuses on celebrating the over-the-top nature of action movie legends, creating a playful atmosphere that immediately sets it apart from more serious shooters.

The game's central concept revolves around recreating the kinds of missions and scenarios commonly seen in iconic action blockbusters. Players take control of a roster of action-inspired characters and fight through enemy-infested environments packed with danger and destruction. The presentation is intentionally humorous, with countless references to classic action tropes. From heavily armed commandos to cybernetic law enforcers, the cast feels like a tribute to the heroes that defined an era of action entertainment. This nostalgic approach gives the game a strong identity and provides much of its charm.

Gameplay is built around accessible twin-stick shooting mechanics that are easy to learn but remain entertaining thanks to the relentless pace. Players battle large groups of enemies while collecting weapons, surviving ambushes, and completing objectives across procedurally generated maps. The randomized level design ensures that no two runs are exactly alike, helping maintain replayability. Missions often involve eliminating enemy forces, rescuing objectives, or surviving intense firefights, all while navigating chaotic battlefields where danger can emerge from every direction.

One of the game's strongest features is its wide selection of weapons and unlockable content. As players progress, they gain access to new firearms, explosives, characters, and upgrades that encourage experimentation. Each character possesses different strengths and weaknesses, allowing players to tailor their playstyle to their preferences. Some heroes excel in durability, while others prioritize speed or offensive power. This variety helps keep the gameplay engaging even after multiple sessions and gives players reasons to continue unlocking additional content.

Visually, Tango Fiesta succeeds in capturing the colorful, exaggerated feel of classic arcade action games. The environments are vibrant and filled with explosive effects that constantly reinforce the game's energetic tone. Character animations and enemy encounters are designed to support the nonstop action, while the soundtrack complements the gameplay with high-energy music that enhances the excitement. Although the graphics are not cutting-edge, the art direction effectively supports the game's nostalgic theme and arcade-inspired personality.

Cooperative multiplayer is where the game reaches its full potential. Supporting up to four players, Tango Fiesta becomes significantly more entertaining when shared with friends. Coordinating attacks, reviving teammates, and battling through overwhelming enemy forces creates memorable moments that embody the spirit of action movies. The cooperative focus adds a social dimension that greatly increases the game's replay value and often produces the most enjoyable experiences the game has to offer.

Despite its strengths, the game does have limitations. The mission structure can become repetitive after extended play sessions, as many objectives revolve around similar combat-focused tasks. While procedural generation helps reduce predictability, it cannot completely eliminate the sense of repetition that eventually develops. Additionally, players looking for deep strategic systems or extensive character progression may find the experience somewhat simplistic compared to more modern roguelike shooters and action games.

The narrative is intentionally lightweight and serves primarily as a framework for humor and action movie references. Those seeking a complex story may find little substance beyond the jokes and homage-filled dialogue. However, this approach is consistent with the game's design philosophy. Tango Fiesta is less concerned with storytelling and more focused on delivering an entertaining, explosive playground inspired by the action films that influenced its creation.

Overall, Tango Fiesta is a fun and energetic shooter that successfully captures the spirit of classic action cinema through arcade-style gameplay, cooperative mayhem, and a healthy sense of humor. While repetitive mission design and limited depth prevent it from reaching the top tier of the genre, its personality, nostalgic appeal, and enjoyable multiplayer action make it a worthwhile experience for fans of twin-stick shooters and retro action movies. It may not reinvent the formula, but it delivers enough explosive entertainment to keep players engaged, especially when enjoyed alongside friends.

Rating: 7/10
